texts.preamble: Vinothini Rajvel vs Universal Shampo General on 24 November, 2020 In The Court Of Small Causes (Scch23) At Bengaluru Dated This The 24th Day Of November 2020 Present: Smt.Ashwini M. Hattiholi (B.Com., Ll.B), Xxi Addl. Scj & Acmm Member Mact, Bengaluru. Mvc. No.5777/2018
texts.facts: * * * JUDGMENT This claim petition is filed under section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/ from the respondents on account of the injuries sustained by the petitioner in a Road Traffic accident that occurred on 23.8.2018. 2. It is the case of the petitioner that on 23.8.2018 at about 8.45 p.m., when she was travelling slowly and steadily in front of Veerasandra signal Petrol bunk, Hosur service road, Bengaluru, on her Two wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA51EZ5740, at that time the driver of Canter bearing Reg.No.KA51 A1898 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner, without caring for human safety and thereby dashed against the petitioner's vehicle. Due to this SCCH23 3 MVC No.5777/2018 impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained injuries all over her body. Hence she was taken for treatment to Sparsh & Blossom hospitals, wherein Xrays were taken, fracture was detected and the doctors opined that the petitioner should be operated as the injuries are grievous in nature. Though the petitioner has taken best available treatment, she is still suffering from disability. That she has spent more than 2 lakhs towards hospitalization and other incidental expenses. She was working as a Fashion designer and earning a sum of Rs.25,000/ p.m. Due to the accident she has lost all her income. In fact the petitioner was the sole bread earner in her family and all her family members were dependant on her for their food, clothing and shelter. That the petitioner was hale and healthy at the time of accident. However due to the accident she not only lost all her income but has also suffered lot of physical and mental stress. The first respondent being the insurer and the second one being the owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to her along with interest @ 12% p.a. 3. Second respondent was placed exparte. First respondent/Insurance company resisted the claim petition SCCH23 4 MVC No.5777/2018 by filing written statement. It denied the petition averments in toto. Inter alia contended that the petition is bad for nonjoinder of necessary parties namely the owner of two wheeler bearing No.KA51EZ5740 and its insurer as the alleged accident took place on account of head on collision between the two wheeler bearing No. KA51 EZ5740 and Canter bearing Reg.No.KA51A1898. In fact asserted that the said accident occurred on account of sole negligence on the part of the driver of Two wheeler bearing Reg. No.KA 51EZ5740. The Insurance company however admitted the issuance of policy to the Canter bearing Reg.No.KA51 A1898 vide policy No.2315/56254107/02/000 valid from 17.6.2018 to 16.6.2019, but disowned its liability. Further specifically claimed that the Investigation Officer failed to forward the copy of the report of accident to the jurisdictional claim Tribunal and also to it as required u/s 158(6) of IMV Act. Under these circumstances prayed to dismiss the petition with costs. During evidence, the petitioner got herself examined as P.W.1. Ex's.P1 to P9 were marked. Dr.Nagaraj B.N S/o Late B.K.N.Swamy, Orthopaedic surgeon & Medico Legal Consultant at Sparsh Hospital Team, Bengaluru, was examined as PW.2 and Ex.P10 & 11 were marked through this witness. On the other hand, respondent No.1 did not choose to adduce evidence.
texts.arguments: 9. In addition to this in a claim for compensation u/s 166 of MV Act 1988, the claimant has to prove the accident only on Preponderance of probabilities and Standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required, as per the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in a decision reported in 2011 SAR (Civil) 319 between Kusum & Others V/s Sathbir and others. The Court must keep this distinction in mind". 10. Reference in this connection may also be made to the decision of the Apex Court in AIR 2009 SC 2819 (Bimla Devi & others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation & others) , wherein it has been held that in a Road accident, the strict principles of proof as in a Criminal case are not attracted. Relevant portion of the said decision is reproduced as follows: SCCH23 10 MVC No.5777/2018 "15. As far as the rate of interest on the award amount is concerned , relying upon the principle laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Municipal Corporation of Delhi V/s Association of Victims of Upahaar Tragedy
